nodes.content: Learn classifiers that reject shifting spurious cues without environment labels while preserving stable predictive features specific to minority groups.
requirements: Specify identifiability conditions distinguishing unstable shortcuts from stable minority-specific signals.
Improve worst-group accuracy ≥5 percentage points over ERM while losing ≤1 percentage point overall.

nodes.content: Train latent-subgroup invariant predictors using shortcut-varying, minority-signal-preserving augmentations; target 5-point worst-group gains with ≤1-point overall loss versus ERM.
What observable augmentation-consistency and subgroup-support conditions distinguish shifting shortcuts from stable minority-specific cues without environment labels?
With label overlap and two independent shortcut interventions per subgroup, stable minority cues retain conditional label association; shortcut associations vanish.
Cross background-scene swaps with independent palette edits on Waterbirds; check label overlap and conditional cue–label stability in inferred subgroups.
Create crossed Waterbirds scene-swap/palette-edit views; test label overlap and subgroup-conditional label associations for background, palette, and morphology.
On Waterbirds, despite ≥30 examples per label and independent edits, background–label AUC remained 0.73 within inferred subgroups.
With verified label-preserving shortcut-only edits and minority counterfactual overlap, shortcut-induced score changes identify instability; invariant morphology retains minority signal.
Audit 200 foreground-masked Waterbirds scene swaps for label fidelity and minority counterfactual overlap; compare background-logit sensitivity against morphology-label AUC.
Waterbirds: 97% of 200 swaps preserved labels; minority counterfactual overlap reached 84%; background/morphology logit shifts were 0.41/0.03.
Adopt audited scene-swap sensitivity over subgroup association: background AUC remained 0.73, while morphology logit shifts were only 0.03.
Cross scene swaps with palette edits; stratify inferred Waterbirds subgroups by swap sensitivity, checking label overlap and cue–label AUC.
Waterbirds audit table v1 records crossed edits, inferred subgroups, label-overlap counts, and cue–label AUC by swap-sensitivity stratum.
How should scene-swap penalties be weighted across inferred subgroups to raise worst-group accuracy without suppressing minority morphology?
Train Waterbirds models with subgroup-weighted scene-swap penalties and foreground-consistency loss; compare worst-group and overall accuracy against ERM.
On Waterbirds, penalties raised worst-group accuracy from 72.0% to 77.4%, but overall accuracy fell from 96.1% to 94.8%.
Add swap-invariant minority residual heads to frozen ERM; gate corrections by audited scene-swap sensitivity, preserving baseline predictions elsewhere.
Audit minority overlap and scene-swap fidelity; train gated invariant residuals on Waterbirds; test ≥5-point worst-group gain, ≤1-point overall loss.
Use audit table v1 to select Waterbirds strata with ≥30 samples per label; train swap-invariant, sensitivity-gated residuals on frozen ERM.
Waterbirds residual-head checkpoint v1 contains frozen ERM weights, subgroup-gated correction heads, and sensitivity thresholds selected from audit table v1.
Benchmark checkpoint v1 against ERM on held-out Waterbirds worst-group and overall accuracy; verify audit table v1 swap fidelity and overlap.
On held-out Waterbirds, gated residuals raised worst-group accuracy from 72.0% to 78.1%; overall accuracy fell from 96.1% to 95.5%.
Adopt gated residuals for Waterbirds: worst-group accuracy improved 6.1 points with 0.6-point overall loss, supported by 97% label-preserving swaps.
Run paired Waterbirds bootstrap comparing scene-swap penalties with residual-head checkpoint v1 on worst-group, overall, and minority-morphology accuracy.
Waterbirds paired bootstrap: λ=0.15 penalties achieved 77.2% worst-group and 95.3% overall versus ERM’s 72.0%/96.1%; minority-morphology accuracy matched residuals at 86%.
Does gate misrouting erase residual-head gains when unseen minority backgrounds show low scene-swap sensitivity?
On unseen minority backgrounds, gate recall below 70% reduces residuals’ worst-group gain below 5 points versus ERM.
Evaluate checkpoint v1 on unseen Waterbirds minority backgrounds; sweep gate thresholds, recording minority gate recall and worst-group gain versus ERM.
On unseen Waterbirds minority backgrounds, 65% gate recall yielded 74.3% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 69.0%.
Blend λ=0.15 invariant and gated-residual models using audited counterfactual overlap, retaining minority morphology without relying solely on sensitivity gates.
On held-out Waterbirds, overlap-weighted blending will exceed 78.1% worst-group accuracy while retaining ≥95.1% overall and ≥86% minority-morphology accuracy.
Calibrate overlap-weighted blends using audit table v1 validation strata; test held-out Waterbirds worst-group, overall, and minority-morphology accuracy.
On held-out Waterbirds, overlap-weighted blending reached 79.0% worst-group, 95.3% overall, and 86.4% minority-morphology accuracy.
Adopt overlap-weighted blend: 79.0% worst-group and 95.3% overall; retain residual component, which gained 5.3 points despite 65% gate recall.
Does overlap-weighted blending retain a ≥5-point worst-group gain on unseen minority backgrounds with <50% counterfactual overlap?
Stress-test the adopted blend on unseen Waterbirds minority backgrounds with <50% counterfactual overlap; compare worst-group and overall accuracy against ERM.
Construct unseen-background Waterbirds split with <50% minority counterfactual overlap; benchmark adopted blend and ERM on worst-group and overall accuracy.
Waterbirds audit table v2 extends v1 with unseen-background split IDs, minority overlap (<50%), swap-fidelity flags, and blend-versus-ERM accuracy.
Validate audit table v2 split membership and swap fidelity; recompute blend-versus-ERM worst-group and overall accuracy for <50% overlap.
On 43%-overlap unseen Waterbirds, blending achieved 75.1% versus 69.0% ERM worst-group, with 94.2% versus 94.8% overall accuracy.
On unseen minority backgrounds, residual-head worst-group gains remain ≥5 points at 65% gate recall but fall below 5 at <45%.
Using audit table v2 unseen-background splits, sweep residual-head gates across 35–70% minority recall; compare worst-group gains against ERM.
On unseen Waterbirds, residual heads gained 5.3 points at 65% gate recall, but 3.8 points at 40%.
Replace sensitivity-only routing with morphology-consistency soft gates and invariant fallback for low-overlap minorities, using audited label-preserving swaps.
Can morphology-consistency gates restore ≥5-point worst-group gains when sensitivity-gate recall falls below 45%, without exceeding 1-point overall loss?
Calibrate morphology-consistency gates on audit table v2; compare worst-group and overall accuracy against ERM at 40% sensitivity-gate recall.
Using audit table v2, benchmark morphology-consistency-gated invariant fallback against overlap-weighted blending on Waterbirds worst-group/overall accuracy at 40% gate recall.
At 40% gate recall, morphology-gated fallback scored 76.2% worst-group and 94.3% overall; blending scored 75.1%/94.2%, ERM 69.0%/94.8%.
Adopt morphology-gated fallback over blending at 40% gate recall: worst-group accuracy rises 1.1 points, with 0.5-point ERM-relative overall loss.
Audit CelebA shortcut-only edits and minority overlap, then test adopted fallback for ≥5-point worst-group gain and ≤1-point overall loss.
Apply audit table v2’s fidelity-and-overlap protocol to 200 CelebA gender-presentation edits; verify Blond_Hair labels and minority counterfactual support.
CelebA Blond_Hair audit v1 records 200 gender-presentation edits, label-fidelity flags, minority counterfactual overlap, and subgroup-support counts.
Validate CelebA audit v1 label fidelity and overlap; benchmark calibrated morphology-gated fallback against ERM at 40% gate recall.
At 40% gate recall, CelebA fallback scored 76.0% worst-group/91.2% overall versus ERM’s 70.5%/91.8%; edit fidelity was 94%, overlap 42%.
Retain morphology-gated fallback over residual-only gating: CelebA gains 5.5 worst-group points with 0.6 overall loss at 40% recall.
Revise residual-only adoption: use morphology-gated invariant fallback below 45% gate recall; retain residual heads otherwise.
